Above: A long but superb season has come from 400 metre man Robert Milner. As early as April 18th he clocked 40.0 for a 300 at Tooting and then, as the summer wore, on he chipped away at his one lap times with his best of 53.6 coming in June at Kingsmeadow. He was "Man of the Match at Tonbridge, placed 3rd in the South of England Boys' Champs in 53.92, won the Inter-County match at Battersea and placed 2nd in the Southern Inter-Counties at Hayes in late August with 53.7.

Youth Rob Milner was another winner, equalling our best on record for an under 17 competing over 91.4cm barriers ... and so it went on until it was finally declared that the Belgrave Juniors had won their first ever league match - and Scott Thompson, surprise, surprise, got man of the match to boot.

Considering that Rob Milner is a first year youth, he runs a mighty mature 400 hurdles. Whatever the competition he seems to find his way into the frame and here at Battersea, racing in under 20 conditions (which means higher barriers) he came away with a fine victory and a further reduction on our under 17 record.

Yet another Belgrave best came from Rob Milner. Even so, he was a little unfortunate as his heat time of 57.31, 8th fastest in the whole of the first round, placed him only 3rd in his race and he had to be content with a performance which erased Alasdair Grant's name from the list.
♦ Gareth Allison, who hurdled for us in the late eighties, is still the holder of our under-20 110m hurdles record although he lost his under-17 400m hurdles record to Rob Milner last summer.

Now in the U17 age group, 400 metre man Robert Milner is branching out into the long hurdle race. After a silver medal winning 58.6 in the Surrey Championships the previous day he lined up here at Battersea with another improvement in mind.

This time, when Robert Milner ran the 400m hurdles he did not fall, thus he returned to his winning form, and Gavin Mason won the B race. After equalling the U13 1500m Club Record at the last meeting, Olivier Bazin broke it by nearly two seconds, gaining victory in the process.

The hard luck story of the champs was that of 400 metre hurdler Robert Milner. A possible winner, he over rotated at a hurdle going into the back straight and fell badly, lying on the deck for a considerable length of time before recovering his composure and getting up to finish a battered and disappointed 4th.
Pictured racing over 200 metres for a change, at Aldershot in the National Junior League, Rob Milner took nearly a whole second off his 400m hurdles Club Record in 1994 with 56.39.

○ Rob Milner is collecting claims to fame. He's got two so far - sat on the toilet at Crystal Palace after Frankie Fredericks had used it and took Du'aine Ladejo's place in the Gold Cup final 4x400 relay.
Left: New under 17 Club Record holder at 56.39 and 10th best in the country for his age, Rob Milner also competed regularly over the 91.4cm barriers and set a Club Best for a 17 year-old of 58.3.

A gutsy performance came from Rob Milner in the long hurdles race. Rob has hardly had the best of preparation for the '94 season, what with appendicitis and shin splints, but his 56.39 here not only gave him 3rd place, it reduced his Club Record by virtually one whole second.
